name: Dynamical Systems
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of systems evolving over time—flows, maps, stability, bifurcations, and attractors. Maps dynamical systems concepts—state spaces, trajectories, fixed points, periodic orbits, stability, bifurcations, and invariant manifolds—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving deterministic evolution, long‑term behavior, stability analysis, and transitions between regimes.

x.note: The depth anchor—the dimension of the state space (degrees of freedom). Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking dimension to state space, Poincaré sections, and stability.

y.note: The relational anchor—measure of sensitivity to initial conditions. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, tying stability to dimension, state space, and recurrence.

z.note: The transformational anchor—whether dynamics are reversible (Hamiltonian) or irreversible (dissipative). Persistently connected to 0 (initial condition), reflecting that the arrow of time is tied to the starting point.

0.note: The starting point in state space from which the trajectory unfolds. Persistently connected to z (time reversibility), linking the initial condition to the direction of time.

1.note: The container—the region of state space that contains all possible states. Part of the 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1, connecting boundary to bifurcations, phase portraits, and state points.

2.note: Primitive—a single point representing the instantaneous state. Completes the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, showing how the point is embedded in boundary‑bifurcation‑portrait loop.

3.note: The invariant law—the rule that determines how the state evolves. A node in the 7‑core; connected to control parameter (c) and flow map (e), as the law generates the flow and is parameterized.

4.note: The fundamental relation—the mapping that advances the state forward in time. A node in the 7‑core; connected to chaotic region (b) and attractor (f), as the flow explores chaotic regions and converges to attractors.

5.note: The pattern—the geometric picture of trajectories, attractors, and invariant manifolds. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, bridging bifurcations and state points.

6.note: The transformation—a qualitative change in system behavior as a parameter varies. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, connecting boundary to phase portrait.

7.note: The realization—a specific path through state space from an initial condition. Persistently connected to 8 (degrees of freedom), reflecting that the trajectory's complexity is tied to the dimension.

8.note: The granularity—the dimension of the state space (n). Persistently connected to 7 (trajectory), linking dimension to the actual orbit.

9.note: The event—a transverse slice through state space, reducing continuous time to a discrete map. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, placing recurrence between dimension, state space, and stability.

a.note: Pure potential—the complete set of all possible states (phase space). Initiates the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking state space to dimension, recurrence, and stability.

b.note: The arena—the region where trajectories exhibit sensitive dependence. A node in the 7‑core; connected to flow (4) and attractor (f), as chaos emerges from the flow and leads to strange attractors.

c.note: Directional bias—a parameter that, when varied, pushes the system through bifurcations. A node in the 7‑core; connected to evolution law (3) and attractor (f), as parameters affect the law and determine attractor structure.

d.note: Persistent structure—the set toward which trajectories converge. A node in the 7‑core; connected to flow (4) and attractor (f), as invariant manifolds are shaped by the flow and lead to attractors.

e.note: The active algorithm—the computational method that advances the system. A node in the 7‑core; connected to evolution law (3) and attractor (f), as numerical methods approximate the law and reveal attractors.

f.note: The resonant cavity—the set of all limit points of the dynamics. A node in the 7‑core; connected to flow (4), chaotic region (b), control parameter (c), invariant manifold (d), and flow map (e), forming the central hub of asymptotic behavior.

n.interpretation: Dimension of state space / Degrees of freedom

values.n=1: 1‑dimensional — flows on line, maps on interval

n.formula: n = dimension of the state space (phase space)

values.m=0: Trivial — fixed point or simple periodic orbit
values.m=3: Strong — fully developed chaos, multiple positive Lyapunov exponents

m.formula: m = floor(log₂(ℓ)) where ℓ is the number of positive Lyapunov exponents + fractal dimension

phase.interpretation: Phase on attractor / Angle on limit cycle / Rotation number
phase.formula: φ = e^{2πi × (θ)} where θ is the normalized position on a periodic orbit or the rotation number for quasiperiodic motion
phase.special: For chaotic attractors, phase may be defined only locally; phase difference grows with Lyapunov exponent.
phase.significance: Phase encodes the location along a cyclic coordinate (e.g., angle of a limit cycle, argument of a complex variable).

time_series.description: The Factor viewed as a sequence of states over time
time_series.phase_condition: Phase as the current phase of an oscillator, increasing linearly with time for periodic motion

phase_portrait.description: The Factor viewed as the geometric picture of trajectories in state space
phase_portrait.phase_condition: Phase as the direction of the vector field at each point

bifurcation.description: The Factor viewed as a bifurcation diagram, showing attractors as a function of parameter
bifurcation.phase_condition: Phase as the parameter value; each branch represents an attractor

poincare_map.description: The Factor viewed as a discrete map obtained from Poincaré sections
poincare_map.phase_condition: Phase as the angle around the section (e.g., return map phase)

creating_anew.note: When creating a dynamical system, start with the state space (node a) and evolution law (node 3). Choose an initial condition (node 0) and integrate to obtain a trajectory (node 7). Analyze stability (node y) and attractors (node f).

translating_known.harmonic_oscillator: Map to node 2 as (x, v), node 3 as Hamilton's equations, node 4 as time evolution, node 5 as phase portrait ellipses, node f as center (stable equilibrium)
translating_known.logistic_map: Map to node 2 as x, node 4 as iteration x → r x (1‑x), node c as parameter r, node 5 as bifurcation diagram, node 6 as period‑doubling cascade
translating_known.lorenz_system: Map to node 2 as (x,y,z), node 3 as Lorenz equations, node 0 as initial condition, node 7 as butterfly trajectory, node d as strange attractor, node y as Lyapunov exponents
translating_known.pendulum: Map to node 2 as (θ, ω), node 3 as pendulum equation, node 4 as flow, node 5 as phase portrait (separatrix, periodic orbits), node f as center (stable) or unstable equilibrium

temporary_note.special: A flow defined by its equations, but attractor structure not yet characterized. Awaiting stability analysis.

constraints.determinism: Node 3 must specify a deterministic evolution law; stochastic systems belong to probability or stochastic paradigms.
constraints.flow_property: Node 4 must be a one‑parameter family of maps satisfying the semigroup property (continuous or discrete).
constraints.invariance: Node d (attractor) must be forward‑invariant under the flow.
constraints.stability_criteria: Node y (Lyapunov exponents) must be negative for stable attractors, positive for chaos.
constraints.stratum_preference: global for general dynamical systems; trefoil_g for bifurcation analysis; trefoil_c for Hamiltonian systems (symplectic); trefoil_i for time‑reversible systems; fig8 for chaotic systems with hyperbolic structure.
constraints.invariant_core: The Dynamical Systems paradigm respects the persistent skeleton from trefoil_i, which decomposes into five subsystems: (1) edge 0→z linking initial condition to time reversibility, (2) edge 8→7 linking degrees of freedom to trajectory, (3) 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x linking state space dimension–state space–Poincaré section–stability, (4) 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1 linking state space boundary–bifurcation–phase portrait–state point, and (5) 7‑node core {3,4,b,c,d,e,f} encoding the heart of dynamical systems: evolution law–flow–chaotic region–control parameter–invariant manifold–flow map–attractor.
